# PromQL notes:

Every query on the dashboard, with what it computes. 

**AI usage:** the PromQL and the regex in the dashboard were generated by Claude. In short form, the part that produced these queries was:

> PromQL for a Grafana dashboard on a Streamlit image-captioning app: health, throughput, latency percentiles, client breakdown, host CPU/memory/disk/network, and panels that correlate app load with host CPU.

That quote is a summary of the intent, not the verbatim prompt. A dashboard JSON file cannot hold comments, so the
explanation of every query lives in this file instead. Regex used in queries: `fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs"`
(real disks only) and `device!~"lo|veth.*|br-.*|docker.*"` (physical network interface only).

Hand-check method for the rate and ratio queries: take two points from the raw counter in the Prometheus
UI (`Graph` tab, e.g. `captioning_images_processed_total`), subtract and divide by the seconds between them, and
compare with what the panel shows. For `histogram_quantile`, look at the raw `_bucket` series and find the bucket where
the cumulative count crosses q x total.

## Captioning app

```promql
up{job="captioning_app"}
```

`up` is 1 when the last scrape of the job worked and 0 when it failed. Stop the app and it flips to 0 within one scrape (5 s).

## node_exporter

```promql
up{job="node"}
```

Same idea as the app status, for the `node` job.

## Model loaded

```promql
max(captioning_model_loaded)
```

Gauge set to 1 right after `from_pretrained()` returns. `max()` just collapses the single series.

## Firing alerts

```promql
count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing"}) or vector(0)
```

Prometheus writes a synthetic series `ALERTS` for every pending/firing alert. `count()` over the firing ones; `or vector(0)` makes it show 0 instead of 'No data' when nothing fires.

## Active requests

```promql
sum(captioning_active_requests)
```

Gauge incremented on request entry and decremented on exit (`track_inprogress`). Summed over the mode label.

## Failed images (last 5 min)

```promql
sum(rate(captioning_images_processed_total{status="error"}[5m])) / clamp_min(sum(rate(captioning_images_processed_total[5m])), 1e-9)
```

errors/s divided by all images/s over 5 m. The 5 m window cancels out in the ratio. `clamp_min(..., 1e-9)` avoids 0/0 when nothing is running (result is then 0).

## Throughput (images per second, by mode)

```promql
sum by (mode) (rate(captioning_images_processed_total{status="success"}[$__rate_interval]))
```

`rate()` turns the ever-growing counter into a per-second speed averaged over `$__rate_interval` (>= 4 scrapes). `sum by (mode)` merges client labels.

## Inference latency percentiles (seconds per image)

```promql
histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(captioning_inference_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))
```
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(captioning_inference_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))
```
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(captioning_inference_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))
```

`_bucket` series hold cumulative counts per upper bound `le`. Rate of each bucket, summed over labels, then `histogram_quantile` interpolates linearly inside the bucket where the q-th fraction falls. Accuracy is limited by bucket width.

## Inference latency distribution (heatmap)

```promql
sum by (le) (increase(captioning_inference_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval]))
```

`increase()` of each cumulative bucket; Grafana subtracts neighbouring buckets (format=heatmap) to get per-bucket counts.

## Average time per request (log scale)

```promql
sum by (mode) (rate(captioning_request_duration_seconds_sum[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (mode) (rate(captioning_request_duration_seconds_count[$__rate_interval]))
```

Summary exposes `_sum` (total seconds) and `_count` (requests). rate(sum)/rate(count) = average seconds per request in the window.

## Errors per minute (by type)

```promql
sum by (error_type) (rate(captioning_errors_total[1m])) * 60
```

Per-second error rate multiplied by 60 to get per-minute, which is easier to read when errors are rare.

## Image size and caption length

```promql
sum(rate(captioning_caption_chars_sum[1m])) / sum(rate(captioning_caption_chars_count[1m]))
```
```promql
sum(rate(captioning_image_megapixels_sum[1m])) / sum(rate(captioning_image_megapixels_count[1m]))
```

Two Summaries, each divided as sum/count over 1 minute, giving a windowed mean.

## Images processed per client IP (since app start)

```promql
topk(10, sum by (client_ip) (captioning_client_images_total))
```

Counter summed per client IP (browser/mode merged). `topk(10)` keeps the 10 biggest.

## Requests per session (since app start)

```promql
topk(10, sum by (session_id) (captioning_requests_total))
```

Same pattern as above on the `session_id` label of the request counter.

## Images processed per browser (since app start)

```promql
sum by (browser) (captioning_client_images_total)
```

Counter summed over the browser label.

## Host CPU usage (%)

```promql
100 * (1 - avg(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])))
```
```promql
100 * avg(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="iowait"}[$__rate_interval]))
```

node_exporter gives cumulative CPU seconds per core and mode. rate(idle) is the fraction of each core that was idle; avg across cores, then 100*(1-idle) = busy%.

## Host memory used (%)

```promql
100 * (1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes)
```
```promql
100 * max(captioning_process_resident_memory_bytes) / max(node_memory_MemTotal_bytes)
```

MemAvailable is the kernel's estimate of memory that can be allocated without swapping, so used = 1 - available/total. App RSS is divided by the same total to share the % axis. `max()` on both sides strips their different job/instance labels so the division can match.

## Disk space used on / (%)

```promql
100 * (1 - max(node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs"}) / max(node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/",fstype!~"tmpfs|overlay|squashfs"}))
```

used% = 100*(1 - avail/size). The regex excludes virtual filesystems so only the real disk matches. `max()` only picks one series if several matched.

## Disk throughput (bytes per second)

```promql
sum(rate(node_disk_read_bytes_total[$__rate_interval]))
```
```promql
sum(rate(node_disk_written_bytes_total[$__rate_interval]))
```

Cumulative byte counters differentiated with rate() and summed over devices.

## Network throughput (bytes per second)

```promql
sum(rate(node_network_receive_bytes_total{device!~"lo|veth.*|br-.*|docker.*"}[$__rate_interval]))
```
```promql
sum(rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total{device!~"lo|veth.*|br-.*|docker.*"}[$__rate_interval]))
```

The `device!~` regex drops loopback, virtual ethernet pairs and docker bridges so we only count the physical NIC.

## Throughput vs host CPU

```promql
sum(rate(captioning_images_processed_total{status="success"}[$__rate_interval]))
```
```promql
100 * (1 - avg(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])))
```

Both queries explained above, plotted together on two axes so spikes can be lined up by eye.

## p95 latency vs host CPU

```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(captioning_inference_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))
```
```promql
100 * (1 - avg(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])))
```

Same percentile query as in section 2, next to host CPU.

## Concurrency vs host CPU

```promql
sum(captioning_active_requests)
```
```promql
captioning_inference_queue_waiting
```
```promql
100 * (1 - avg(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])))
```

Two gauges straight from the app, host CPU as before.

## App CPU share vs host CPU

```promql
captioning_process_cpu_percent
```
```promql
100 * (1 - avg(rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval])))
```

psutil `cpu_percent()/n_cpu` inside the app (so 100 means all cores) compared with node_exporter's host-wide number.
